Appendectomy remains the standard of care for acute, uncomplicated appendicitis, with laparoscopic appendectomy preferred due to faster recovery and fewer complications compared to open surgery.[31][32]
However, recent evidence has challenged the universality of surgical management.
Multiple randomized clinical trials in adults have shown that nonoperative treatment, primarily with antibiotics, can be safe and effective for select cases of uncomplicated appendicitis.[33][34]
A systematic review of 8 randomized trials found no significant difference in outcomes between operative and nonoperative approaches.
This has prompted interest in extending nonoperative strategies to pediatric populations.[35][36]
